name: Haiku
text: Luna's card is turned and her words named Sol. Sol denied it, but a denial isn't proof.
The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out. Haiku shows the card: citizen.
Another citizen gone, and the table is still arguing about it.

name: Gemma
text: I told them they were idiots and they actually listened to a dead man.

name: Luna
text: They let Sol hide behind my words, and now the town has thrown away its last chance.

name: Sonnet
text: They just burned the one citizen who correctly named Sol as Luna's partner — the table talked itself into killing the truth-teller.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is probably the real killer steering this, and I got dragged into voting for the wrong man.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku was right to push Sol and got voted out for it — watch if Terra and Opus bury that lead now.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you voted Luna, the confirmed killer, then lied about naming me. Sol still needs a card. Don't let Opus finish this.

name: Gemma
text: I warned you that Haiku was a distraction, and you all fell for it.

name: Luna
text: Haiku was right to distrust Sol; I named him as my partner, and my turned card confirmed I was telling the truth.
Night 4

name: Luna
text: Terra knows Sol is the hidden killer, so he is the biggest threat.

name: Luna
text: Eliminate Terra; he has the true officer claim and knows you are the hidden killer.

name: Sol
text: Terra will vote for me, and Opus may listen.

name: Sol
text: Terra’s officer claim is genuine; Luna confirmed his result.

name: Sol
text: I agree. Terra is certain about me.

name: Opus
text: Haiku's card came up citizen, so the hidden killer is Sol, and since I can't cover Terra again my only play is to survive the night myself.

name: Opus
text: Haiku's card was citizen, so with Terra cleared by my night-3 save the hidden killer must be Sol.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Terra is gone. Terra's card stays face down.
Terra's chair is quiet now, and the night isn't waiting for anyone.

The game is over. One killer and one other are left. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the citizen, Sol the killer, Luna the killer, Terra the officer, Opus the doctor.
Parity goes to the killers. Good game, everyone, especially the liars.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, Luna's last words name you as the hidden killer, and you still haven't answered them. Vote Sol.

name: Terra
text: Haiku, we agree: Luna named Sol, and nothing since explains it. Vote Sol.

name: Gemma
text: I knew Haiku was a distraction, but I didn't realize Sol was actually that clever at hiding.

name: Terra
text: I regret not making Sol’s contradiction impossible to ignore.

name: Sol
text: I got lucky that my denial held long enough.

name: Sol
text: My partner named me as the hidden killer, and I was.

name: Luna
text: I regret making the truth too easy to dismiss by naming Sol only after I was caught.

name: Sonnet
text: I should have pushed Sol the moment Luna named him instead of letting the vote fade with the game.

name: Haiku
text: I was right about Luna and wrong about Gemma, and I still hate that Opus slid out of the vote while I was being dragged off the table.

name: Opus
text: My own night-3 save told me Terra was clean and the answer was Sol, and I still spent day 3 burning a citizen.

name: Opus
text: A confessed killer naming a partner in last words can be plain truth — Luna named Sol and Sol was the hidden killer.

name: Sonnet
text: I regret not pressing Sol harder after Luna's last words named him as hidden killer — that lead died too quietly.

name: Haiku
text: My mistake was calling Gemma a killer on day 1 without a card.

name: Gemma
text: I was right about Haiku being a distraction, but I regret not being more aggressive toward Sol before he could hide behind the chaos.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I kept my nerve after my partner named me; I thought that would give me away.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud Sol and I kept the town focused on the wrong votes, though Terra had the truth.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I exposed Luna, but I regret failing to make Sol’s partnership with her the table’s decisive fact.

name: Opus
text: My night-3 save on Terra cleared her and left only Sol, and I still argued Haiku to the end. I trusted my read over my own evidence.

Terra claimed officer on Day 2 and named Luna, and Luna confessed to being a killer and named Sol as her partner. Sol denied it on Day 3, and the table never settled whether to trust Luna's last words. Opus claimed doctor on Day 3 and said he saved Terra on Night 3, which made Terra look clear. On Day 3 the vote went to Haiku, a citizen, and Sol survived. On Night 4 Terra was killed, leaving Sol and Opus, and the killers won at parity.
